items.title: Anthropic's new prototype proves which model wrote an AI response without exposing its weights
items.summary: Anthropic has released FlashProve, a research prototype that uses cryptography to verify whether an AI response actually came from the claimed model. The system still has significant limitations. The article Anthropic's new prototype proves which model wrote an AI response without exposing its weights appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: GPT-6 Astra sees the matrix and reprograms other AI models directly through their weights
items.summary: MIT researchers show that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can read and deliberately rewrite the weights of other AI models without traditional training. In one experiment, Astra boosted a Qwen model's math accuracy from 7.9 to 48.1 percent by changing just 0.016 percent of its weights. The approach could fundamentally simplify AI optimization but still hits clear limits....

items.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that rogue agents don’t break the law,…
